decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have improved in recent months, but the rise in COVID-19 cases has slowed their recovery.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have shown improvement but have not fully recovered.”

changes.quote: Inflation is elevated, largely reflecting transitory factors.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has risen, largely reflecting transitory factors.”

changes.quote: Since then, the economy has made progress toward these goals.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Since then, the economy has made progress toward these goals, and the Committee will continue to assess progress in coming meetings.”

changes.quote: If progress continues broadly as expected, the Committee judges that a moderation in the pace of asset purchases may soon be warranted.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses.
Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.

The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.61% APR costs about $60.88 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.32% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 2.88% would fall by about $1.60 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.1%, and employers added an average of 750k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 5.2% over the past year (August 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 7.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.95%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.17% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 80%, cut 2%, hike 17%.
